note: Engine cases for the REFUSAL exhibit (refuse.l4; ruling D1, 2026-09-05).
WHAT THESE COVER, and it is the whole point of the exhibit: a decision that
DECLINES TO ANSWER is executed by two real engines, and both agree about
what comes back. Before D1 this file could not exist — the exporter wrote
the L4 text `REFUSE "…"` into a <literalExpression> and KIE 8.44.0.Final
failed to compile the WHOLE model (ERR_COMPILING_FEEL, VERDICT FAILED), so
no case could reach a refusal on any engine.
`null` IS THE EXPECTED VALUE, AND IT IS DECLARED. The harnesses treat a
null answer as a failure BY DEFAULT; an EXPLICIT JSON null in `expect`
licenses it, for that decision and that case only. Every null below is
therefore an assertion that the model declined, not an absence of one.
A REFUSING DECISION IS EVALUATED EVEN WHEN NOTHING REACHES IT, which is
why `no_fee_is_prescribed_before_commencement_on_1983_01_01` is null in
EVERY case including the ones where the floor row does not fire. A DMN
<decision> is a node in a graph, not a branch of an expression: the engine
evaluates it whenever it evaluates the model. That is the fact D-REFUSE's
severity calibration is about, and pinning it here is what stops a later
reading of `the filing fee` = 1000 being mistaken for `the refusal did not
happen`.
TWO INDEPENDENT AXES, and case D separates them: `RULES_EFFECTIVE_DATE` is
the date the LAW is about and gates the fee chain; `the_claim_amount` is
what the CASE is about and gates the discount and the band. Case D asks a
pre-commencement rule date about a large claim, so the fee chain refuses
while the discount and the band answer — a refusal that leaked across the
two axes would fail there and only there.
CASE E STRADDLES COMMENCEMENT ITSELF (the day of, against case C's day
before), which is what pins the closed-low convention on the interval
table's lowest arm. Delete the pair and an off-by-one on `commencement`
passes green.
THE ENUM CASE IS `the_band`. Its <outputValues> declares `null` alongside
the three constructors, because the two engines disagreed without that:
KIE enforces <outputValues> at run time and FAILED the decision ("Value
null does not match list of allowed values") while zeebe-dmn returned the
null silently. Measured 2026-09-05. The unwidened form is kept as a
negative control in not-ok/refuse-enum-unwidened.dmn so the divergence
cannot come back unnoticed.
ACTIVATION CONTRACT: every expected value below was derived from the L4
SOURCE, not from a DMN engine's own output — a pin regenerated from the
thing it pins is vacuous. `commencement`, `the transition day`, the three
fee arms and the two ladders are read straight off refuse.l4; the nulls
are what L4 says a REFUSE does, which is to stop with the author's reason.
The one value that is NOT derivable from L4 is `the_fee_with_surcharge` in
the refusing cases: L4 never reaches the multiplication, because the
refusal stops evaluation, whereas FEEL has no such notion and computes
`null * 2`. That it is null on both engines is a MEASURED FEEL fact, and
it is stated here rather than passed off as a derivation.
`{"$date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}` is the fixture vocabulary's only way to say
"this is a FEEL date"; both harnesses convert by declared type, never by
appearance.

cases.name: A. the current regime, a large claim — nothing refuses except the refusal itself
B. the original regime, a middling claim
C. THE REFUSAL — the day before commencement, a claim below every floor
D. the two axes pulled apart — the law refuses, the claim does not
E. boundary — commencement day itself: the lowest arm's low end is CLOSED
